subject: general
question: Which of the following comes under the concurrent list?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Forest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution includes subjects that are of interest to both the Union and the States.
 
• Forests are included in the Concurrent List to ensure both state and central governments can make laws regarding their management and conservation.
 
• This inclusion helps in maintaining ecological balance and addresses issues like deforestation and forest conservation more effectively.
 
• Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate on concurrent subjects, but in case of any conflict, the central law prevails.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Police**

 
 
• Police is a subject under the State List. This means that only the state governments have the authority to legislate on matters related to the police.
 
• Each state in India has its own police force and administration.
 
 
 
• **Trade**
 
 
• Trade and commerce within the state are under the State List, while trade and commerce between different states or with foreign countries fall under the Union List.
 
• This division ensures that states can manage their internal trade, while the central government can regulate inter-state and international trade.
 
 
 
• **Defense**
 
 
• Defense is a subject under the Union List, meaning only the central government can legislate on matters related to national defense and security.
 
• This ensures a unified and consistent defense policy for the entire country.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List**
 
 
• The Concurrent List is one of the three lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution that outlines the subjects on which both the state and central governments can legislate.
 
• Subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and forests, among others.
 
• This list aims to ensure cooperative federalism and addresses issues that are of common interest to both the states and the union.
 
• In case of any conflict between central and state laws on a concurrent subject, the central law prevails.
